title_guess: Inflation: meaning, how the rate is calculated, and its types by rate (creeping, walking, galloping, hyper) with Zimbabwe, Germany and Venezuela as real cases
recurring_cast: basket (grocery bag of food, labelled GOODS) and delivery_rider (scooter courier, labelled SERVICES) as the 'goods and services' bundle, 0-91 s
ruler: the 'INFLATION %' scale bar, plain blue, later a green-to-red heat strip, built across 91-253 s
bread_packet (a branded brown-bread pack) as the hyperinflation example, 253-334 s
rupee_note: photo of a 50 rupee note under Today and Tomorrow
world_map in grey with countries lit red and labelled with a year
running_examples: goods and services cost 5000 rupees in 2021 and 5500 in 2022, so the rate is (5500-5000)/5000 x 100 = 10%
10% a year for 20 years: 5000 rupees in 2021 becomes 33,638 rupees in 2041 (checks out: 5000 x 1.1^20 = 33,637.5)
rate bands on one scale: creeping 0-4% (2-4% good), walking 4-10%, galloping 10-50%, hyper above 50%
1,000,000% inflation: a 50 rupee bread packet costs 1419 rupees the next morning; the same 50 rupee note then buys one slice
Zimbabwe 2008: '90 Billion Million %' on screen, bread at 3.5 crore Zimbabwe dollars, a 100,000,000 dollar bearer cheque, currency called worthless

best_moments.why: the same 50 rupee note sits under Today and Tomorrow, and tomorrow's bread packet shrinks to a single slice: money losing value is shown with almost no text
the whole inflation scale repaints from plain blue to a green-to-red heat strip just as the narrator says danger grows with the rate: the verdict of the classification carried by one colour change
the 10% from the formula turns into a curve that bends up from 5000 rupees to 33,638 by 2041: a small rate becomes a big, felt price
the hypothetical '1 Million %' is struck and the real Zimbabwe figure written under it, answering 'is this only hypothetical?' on the number itself
a non-example panel: only eggs got dearer, and the tag 'INFLATION' over them is struck through, showing what the concept is not
walking inflation is added last, as a bracket over the gap between creeping and galloping, which makes 'the warning zone between good and dangerous' visible

weak_moments.why: why creeping is good and why galloping is dangerous are full sentences in coloured text boxes that pop in whole; nothing shows profits, investment or growth
walking inflation's role as an alert for the central bank and the government is about 20 s of speech over a still bar with only a label; no alarm, no central bank on screen
the formula fades in whole and stays still while subtract, divide and multiply by 100 are spoken; no operation lights up on its word

doubtful arithmetic: 1419 rupees equals 50 + 50 x 10,000 / 365, i.e. the year's rise spread evenly over days; with daily compounding 1,000,000% a year is about 2.6% a day, so the next-morning price would be about 51 rupees

facts to check: '90 Billion Million %' (about 9 x 10^16 %) does not match the usually quoted peak estimate for Zimbabwe in late 2008 (about 89.7 sextillion %); notes 'up to 100 million dollars' leaves out the larger notes (up to 100 trillion) issued in early 2009
hyperinflation is shown as '> 50%' on a yearly scale; the common textbook threshold is 50% per month, so the period should be checked and stated
real brand on the bread packet, a real person's portrait on the 50 rupee note photo and a real bearer-cheque photo; BIE will not use these

segments.teaches: inflation is a continuing rise in the general price level of goods and services in the economy; one or two goods getting dearer is not inflation

elements.what: grocery bag of food labelled GOODS
delivery rider on a red scooter labelled SERVICES, joined to goods by '&'
Price against Year axes; three points climb and a red arrow labelled INFLATION rides up along them
box pointing at the arrow: rise in the general price level in the economy
small panel under GOODS with a row of eggs and a note that only one or two goods got dearer
small 'INFLATION' tag on the egg panel, apparently struck through

segments.notes: 4 change events. At 0-1 s a 'like target' counter overlay (channel promotion) sits at bottom-left. The egg panel lives only about 5 s (21.4-26.0); the struck tag lands on 'badh' (23.2 s), 1.2 s before 'inflation nahin' is spoken.
segments.idea: inflation means the general price level of goods and services keeps rising; one or two goods getting dearer is not inflation
segments.shown_as: a grocery bag (goods) and a delivery rider (services) stand beside empty price-year axes; three points climb and a red INFLATION arrow rides up the curve with a callout naming the general price level; then a small egg panel under the goods says only one or two goods got dearer, and its 'INFLATION' tag is struck through

segments.teaches: rate of inflation = (this year's price level - last year's) / last year's x 100; 5000 to 5500 gives 10%

elements.what: INFLATION %
horizontal line with ticks 2021 and 2022
the small goods-and-services bundle standing on each year
price labels '5000 rupees' under 2021 and '5500 rupees' under 2022
(5500 - 5000) / 5000 x 100 = 10%, written beside the title

segments.notes: 5 change events. Each price pops in on its spoken number (5000 at 33.4 s, 5500 at 36.8 s). The whole formula fades in from about 40 s and stays still while subtract (~44 s), divide (~51 s) and multiply by 100 (~53.5 s) are spoken; no step is highlighted. Numbers shown and spoken agree.
segments.idea: the inflation rate is the rise in price divided by the old price, times 100
segments.shown_as: the same goods-and-services bundle stands twice on a timeline, at 2021 tagged 5000 rupees and at 2022 tagged 5500 rupees, each tag popping in on its spoken number; above them the formula fades in with those numbers already in its slots and ends in 10%
segments.example: goods and services 5000 rupees in 2021, 5500 in 2022, so 10%

segments.teaches: 10% inflation a year compounds: what costs 5000 rupees in 2021 costs 33,638 rupees in 2041

elements.what: the 10% formula kept at the top
price axis with 5000 rupees at 2021; a curve bends upward to a dot at 2041; the faded bundle sits behind the curve
red '33638 rupees' on the price axis and a red 2041 tick

segments.notes: 2 change events. 33638 appears about 1 s before it is spoken (79.2 s). The bundle stays faded, so 'the same goods now cost this much' is carried by the label, not by the bundle or a price tag growing.
segments.idea: a steady 10% a year makes the same basket cost almost seven times more after 20 years
segments.shown_as: the timeline turns into a price chart: a curve starts at 5000 rupees in 2021 and bends ever more steeply to a dot at 2041, where a red 33,638 rupees is marked on the price axis, with the faded goods-and-services bundle behind it
segments.example: 5000 rupees at 10% a year for 20 years = 33,638 rupees in 2041

segments.teaches: inflation is named by its rate on one scale: creeping 0-4% (2-4% is good: producers and traders earn reasonable profits, investors invest, growth follows) and galloping 10-50% (dangerous; also called hopping, jumping, running or runaway)

elements.what: INFLATION %
long horizontal blue bar used as a percent ruler with ticks 0%, 4%, 10%, 50% (a number line, not years)
grey bracket under 0-4% with a down-arrow to 'Creeping Inflation'
green note: low inflation of 2-4% is good because producers and traders earn and invest
longer grey bracket under 10-50% with a down-arrow to 'Galloping Inflation'
brown note: 10-50% is dangerous for the economy
three brown bullets with other names: hopping, jumping, running/runaway

segments.notes: 7 change events. Colour code: green text = good, brown = dangerous. Both notes are sentences that pop in whole and are then read out (the 101 s note is read over 101.5-117.6 s). The alias bullets write on one by one as they are spoken (168.8-173.5 s). A 4 s transcript gap (143.7-147.6) falls right after the galloping note appears. The narrator says books differ (10-100%, 10-200%); this is not on screen.
segments.idea: inflation is named by how fast prices rise: a little (creeping) helps the economy, a lot (galloping) is dangerous
segments.shown_as: a long blue bar becomes a percent ruler; a bracket under 0-4% drops an arrow to 'Creeping Inflation' with a green note that 2-4% helps producers earn and invest; later a longer bracket under 10-50% drops to 'Galloping Inflation' with a brown note that it is dangerous, and its three other names write on beneath as they are said

segments.teaches: walking inflation (4-10%) is an alert for the central bank and the government; danger grows as the rate rises; above 50% is hyperinflation, the extreme form, with prices shooting up almost every day

elements.what: short bracket above the 4-10% gap with an up-arrow to 'Walking Inflation'
the whole bar recoloured as a green-to-red heat strip
arrow labelled '> 50%' and a bracket above the red end with an up-arrow to 'Hyper Inflation'
red '[Extreme Form of Inflation]'
red note: prices of goods and services start shooting up almost every day

segments.notes: 6 change events. Walking gets only a label and no note: its 'alert' role (189-208 s) is spoken over a still screen. The heat strip appears at 209.8 s, before 'jaise jaise inflation badh rahi hai' (211.2-212.3 s). The Hyper label appears about 2.4 s before 'hyper' is spoken. Check before reuse: the scale reads '> 50%' as a yearly rate, while the common textbook threshold for hyperinflation is 50% per month.
segments.idea: the further along the scale, the more dangerous: walking (4-10%) is the warning zone, and above 50% is hyperinflation
segments.shown_as: a bracket above the gap between 4% and 10% raises 'Walking Inflation'; then the whole bar repaints from blue into a green-to-red heat strip as danger is said to grow with the rate; an arrow '> 50%' and a bracket over the red end raise 'Hyper Inflation', tagged extreme, with a red note that prices shoot up almost daily
segments.place_change: the scale bar, the backbone of this board, repaints from plain blue to a green-to-red heat strip at 209.8 s, just before 'jaise jaise inflation badh rahi hai' (211.2 s) and 'aur zyada dangerous' (about 214 s)

segments.teaches: in hyperinflation the yearly rate can reach millions of percent and paper money loses value very fast

elements.what: close-up of the red end of the bar: 50% tick, '> 50%' arrow, header 'Hyper Inflation [Extreme Form of Inflation]'
yellow tick at the far right labelled 'Million %'
red box: hyperinflation erodes the value of money very fast

segments.notes: 3 change events. The scale is not in proportion (50% near the left and 'Million %' at the right edge of one screen), so the move suggests distance without true scale. 'Million %' appears 1 s before 'millions' is spoken; the callout lands on 'aisi situation' about 1 s before 'paper money ki value'.
segments.idea: hyperinflation can reach millions of percent a year, and then paper money loses value very fast
segments.shown_as: the camera slides right along the red end of the bar past 50% until a far tick reads 'Million %'; a red callout then says that hyperinflation eats the value of money
segments.example: annual inflation in millions of percent

segments.teaches: at 1,000,000% inflation a 50 rupee bread packet costs 1419 rupees the next morning; seen another way, the same 50 rupee note buys only one slice tomorrow

elements.what: 'INFLATION 1 Million %', later with a red 'HYPER' added in front
line with two ticks, Today and Tomorrow
a branded brown-bread packet at Today and at Tomorrow
price labels '50 rupees' (Today) and '1419 rupees' (Tomorrow)
a 50 rupee note (real portrait on it) placed under each tick, replacing the price labels
a single slice of bread that replaces tomorrow's packet

segments.notes: 9 change events. Doubtful number: 1419 = 50 + 50 x 10,000 / 365 (the year's rise spread evenly per day, not compounded); with daily compounding the next-morning price would be about 51 rupees. The picture idea (same note, one slice) is strong; recompute the number before reuse. 'HYPER' joins the title on the spoken word 'hyper' (280.9 s). Real brand and portrait: BIE will draw its own bread and note.
segments.idea: in hyperinflation the same note buys far less by the next day: money loses value overnight
segments.shown_as: a bread packet stands at Today with 50 rupees and another at Tomorrow with 1419 rupees; then both prices become the same 50 rupee note, and tomorrow's packet shrinks to a single slice of bread, so the note stays the same while what it buys collapses; the title gains a red 'HYPER' as the term is said
segments.example: 1,000,000% a year: bread 50 rupees today, 1419 tomorrow; the 50 rupee note buys one slice

segments.teaches: hyperinflation is real: Zimbabwe in 2008 (90 billion million % on screen), bread at 3.5 crore Zimbabwe dollars, notes of 100 million dollars printed, the currency called worthless

elements.what: grey world map with Zimbabwe dotted red and labelled
red 'HYPER INFLATION' beside Zimbabwe
calendar showing 2008
'1 Million %' struck through, '90 Billion Million %' written under it
the branded bread packet again, with '3.5 Crore Zimbabwe dollar (ZWD)'
a Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe 100,000,000 dollar bearer cheque that replaces the bread
yellow box over the words 'one hundred million dollars' on the note
red line: a news magazine declared Zimbabwe's currency worthless, with 'worthless' highlighted

segments.notes: 8 change events. The map appears about 4 s before 'Zimbabwe' is spoken, while the objection 'kahan hota hoga' is still being voiced. Facts to check before reuse: '90 Billion Million %' does not match the usually quoted peak estimate for late 2008 (about 89.7 sextillion %); 'notes up to 100 million dollars' leaves out larger notes (up to 100 trillion) issued in early 2009; the bread price and the magazine anecdote are not verified here. 314-332 s: one word is stretched over about 13 s in the transcript (a pause) while the screen stays still.
segments.idea: hyperinflation is real: in Zimbabwe in 2008 a bread packet cost crores and even 100-million notes were worthless
segments.shown_as: the world map lights Zimbabwe red under 'HYPER INFLATION 1 Million %'; a 2008 calendar drops in, the hypothetical '1 Million %' is struck and replaced by the real figure; the bread packet returns priced at 3.5 crore Zimbabwe dollars, then gives way to a photo of a 100-million-dollar bearer cheque whose amount is boxed in yellow, and a red line says the currency was declared worthless
segments.example: Zimbabwe 2008: 90 billion million % (as shown), bread 3.5 crore ZWD, 100,000,000 dollar note
